key_insight: A shared PV forecasting model pretrained across sites and horizons enables direct forecasting at unseen stations without station-specific retraining.
engineering_relevance: The framework could reduce model training and maintenance across distributed solar fleets while allowing later adaptation to local operating needs.
method: Formulate forecasting as sequence completion using historical PV power, weather observations, future numerical weather predictions, and time encodings.
Compare forecast-aligned, generic, and mixed reconstruction pretraining objectives.
Use mixed reconstruction to balance forecasting accuracy, robustness to degraded weather forecasts, and downstream adaptation.
evidence_signal: Experiments cover 479 PV stations—340 for model development and 139 spatially held out for zero-shot evaluation—with the mixed-reconstruction model outperforming tested baselines across horizons from 6 hours to 7 days.
watch_item: The abstract reports no numerical performance gains, leaving the practical benefit and reliability under specific deployment conditions to be verified.
paper_title: Foundation-Style Pretraining for Scalable and Transferable Distributed PV Forecasting
